class.name: PhysXVehicle3D
class.brief_description: A PhysX-specific 4-wheel vehicle, powered by PxVehicle2 -- an alternative to the stock, backend-agnostic [VehicleBody3D], not a replacement for it.
class.description: [b]Placement convention:[/b] Redot's own -- the car's nose points toward its local [b]-Z[/b] and the steered axle goes on the more negative Z side; [method get_forward_speed] reads positive while driving nose-first. A model authored facing -Z (the usual Redot case) drops in unchanged. [b]Chassis collision:[/b] exactly one [CollisionShape3D] child with a [BoxShape3D] is used as the real chassis shape (compound shapes are not supported here); the chassis box is a genuine simulation shape, so other bodies collide with the car. [b]Transform contract:[/b] the node's transform follows the chassis every physics tick, but a script write to [member Node3D.global_transform] while live pushes the pose INTO the chassis and zeroes all velocities -- reset/respawn is just setting the transform, RigidBody3D-style. [VehicleBody3D]/[VehicleWheel3D] work on this module already (no PhysX-specific code needed) and stay the right choice for a project that wants to swap physics backends freely. [PhysXVehicle3D] exists for real PxVehicle2 capability that backend-agnostic model structurally can't offer: a real engine torque response, Ackermann steering correction (inner/outer front wheels turn by different angles in a turn), and a real slip-based tire friction curve (grip peaks at a small amount of wheel slip and falls off once the tire is fully sliding/locked, instead of one flat friction number). Node structure mirrors [VehicleBody3D]/[VehicleWheel3D] on purpose: add a [CollisionShape3D] child with a [BoxShape3D] for the chassis, and exactly 4 [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children for the wheels -- exactly 2 of them need [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering] enabled (the front axle). Each wheel's own [member Node3D.position] is where it rests under static load (the same convention [VehicleWheel3D] uses), so a [MeshInstance3D] parented under a wheel tracks the real, live suspension/steering motion automatically, and already sits at the right height in the editor before Play. Drive it every physics tick by setting [member throttle], [member brake], [member steer], and (once actually stopped) [member reverse] -- these use PxVehicleCommandState's own convention ([member throttle]/[member brake] in [code][0, 1][/code], [member steer] in [code][-1, 1][/code]), not [VehicleBody3D]'s raw force/angle convention. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate or fall under gravity.

method.name: get_actor_position
method.description: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own [member Node3D.global_position] (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.

method.name: get_engine_gear
method.description: Current gearbox state: [code]0[/code] = reverse, [code]1[/code] = neutral, [code]2[/code] and up = first gear onward.

method.name: get_forward_speed
method.description: Current speed along the car's own forward axis, in m/s. Positive while driving forward, negative while rolling backward -- a simple way to decide when it is safe to switch [member reverse] on (a real gear should only engage once the car has actually stopped, not while still coasting forward).

method.name: get_linear_velocity
method.description: Current world-space linear velocity of the chassis.

method.name: get_wheel_jounce
method.description: How compressed wheel [param wheel]'s suspension is right now, from [code]0[/code] (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] (fully compressed / bottomed out). [param wheel] is the child index among this node's [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children, in the order they were added -- not a fixed front-left/front-right/rear-left/rear-right order. Useful for tuning [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_stiffness]: resting jounce well under half of [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] leaves real margin before the suspension bottoms out under braking, cornering, or a bump.

method.name: get_wheel_separation
method.description: [code]0[/code] when wheel [param wheel] can reach the ground within its suspension travel. A negative value means the wheel is penetrating the ground even at full compression -- [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] is too short for the current ride height. [param wheel] uses the same child-index convention as [method get_wheel_jounce].

method.name: is_sleeping
method.description: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.

members.member: How much Ackermann steering correction to apply to the front (steering) axle, from [code]0[/code] (both front wheels always turn by the same angle, like [VehicleWheel3D]) to [code]1[/code] (full correction: the inside wheel of a turn steers more sharply than the outside wheel, matching how a real front axle is geometrically linked).
Engine omega fraction of [member engine_max_omega] that triggers a downshift.
Reaction delay of the automatic gearbox before initiating a shift.
Engine omega fraction of [member engine_max_omega] that triggers an upshift.

Brake pedal input, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_brake_torque] of braking torque at each wheel. Set every physics tick from script; does not persist on its own the way a real pedal would.

Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds. The global [code]physics/physx_3d/simulation/allow_sleep[/code] project setting can disable sleeping for all PhysX bodies.

The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when [member center_of_mass_mode] is [code]Custom[/code]. Lowering the Y coordinate can make the vehicle more resistant to rollover. In [code]Auto[/code] mode, the center of mass follows the chassis [CollisionShape3D] child position.
Whether to derive the center of mass from the chassis [CollisionShape3D] position ([code]Auto[/code]) or use [member center_of_mass] directly ([code]Custom[/code]).

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer]. Applies to the chassis only -- the wheels do not have their own collision shapes (their ground contact is handled entirely by the suspension, not by a physical wheel shape touching the road).

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask]. Applies to the chassis box and to what the wheels' own ground raycasts can rest on: a wheel only hits non-area shapes on a layer in this mask (like a [RayCast3D]), so it never rests on an [Area3D]. See [member collision_layer].
Engine angular speed (rad/s) at peak power; the automatic gearbox shifts against this scale.
Peak engine torque used by the gearbox torque curve (see [member use_gearbox]).

Anti-roll bar stiffness connecting the front-left and front-right wheels. A positive value is a real anti-roll bar: it resists the difference in suspension compression between the two wheels, reducing body roll during cornering. A negative value does the opposite -- it amplifies that difference, exaggerating roll instead of resisting it, which is a cheaper and more targeted way to get a more dramatic cornering lean than lowering [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_stiffness] further (that also softens straight-line bump absorption; this only affects side-to-side compression difference). [code]0[/code] disables the bar entirely.
Final drive multiplier applied after the selected gear's ratio.
Seconds a gear change takes (torque interrupted, see [method get_engine_gear]).
Total mass of the vehicle, in kg.

The braking torque applied to each wheel when [member brake] is [code]1[/code]. Higher values stop the wheel's own rotation faster, but do not by themselves determine whether the tire skids once locked -- see [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.tire_friction] for that.

The drive torque applied to every wheel with [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction] enabled when [member throttle] is [code]1[/code] (a real direct-drive response, unlike [member VehicleBody3D.engine_force] which is a raw force value with no torque curve).
The steering angle, in radians, applied to the front axle when [member steer] is [code]1[/code] or [code]-1[/code]. The default (~34°) is a realistic maximum for a real car's front wheels.

The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes. Higher values resist rotation (pitch/yaw/roll) more -- tune the Y (yaw) component if the car turns too eagerly or too sluggishly for its size.

Contact material of the chassis box (the property [RigidBody3D] and [VehicleBody3D] use): its friction, [i]rough[/i], bounce and [i]absorbent[/i] combine with whatever the vehicle touches by the same rule as every PhysX body. Applies to the chassis box only -- tire grip is the wheels' own. Unset, the chassis behaves as it always has (friction [code]1.0[/code], bounce [code]0.0[/code]). Changes -- here or to the assigned material -- apply in place without a rebuild and wake the vehicle.

Same as [member front_anti_roll_stiffness], connecting the rear-left and rear-right wheels instead. Tuning front and rear independently changes handling balance: a stiffer (more positive) front bar relative to the rear tends toward understeer, and vice versa for oversteer -- same real-world relationship a physical anti-roll bar has.

Switches the drivetrain's gear between forward and reverse -- a real gear change (PxVehicle2 has no neutral-coast/instant-reverse shortcut), so [member throttle] in reverse gear still needs to first bring the car to a stop if it was moving forward, same as a real car. Check [method get_forward_speed] before engaging this from a driving script. In engine-drive mode ([member use_gearbox]) this instead commands the reverse gear ([constant GEAR_REVERSE]).
Steering input, [code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_steer_angle] on the front (steering) axle, modified by [member ackermann_strength]. Set every physics tick from script.

The commanded gearbox gear in engine-drive mode ([member use_gearbox]): [constant GEAR_AUTOMATIC] ([code]255[/code], DRIVE -- the autobox picks the forward gears), [constant GEAR_REVERSE] ([code]0[/code]), [constant GEAR_NEUTRAL] ([code]1[/code] -- no drive torque reaches the wheels, the car coasts), or [code]2[/code] and up for a specific forward gear (2 = 1st, 3 = 2nd, ...). Ignored by the direct drivetrain.

Throttle input, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. In direct drive this scales up to [member max_engine_torque] of drive torque at each traction wheel, in whichever direction [member reverse] currently selects; in engine drive it is the engine's accelerator (a magnitude -- the gear picks the direction). Set every physics tick from script.

Engine-drive only: with [member target_gear] left at [constant GEAR_AUTOMATIC], the autobox shifts up/down by engine speed -- above [member autobox_up_ratio] (as a fraction of engine omega over max omega) it shifts up, below [member autobox_down_ratio] it shifts down, waiting at least [member autobox_latency] seconds between shifts. With it off, [member target_gear] is honored verbatim (manual shifting).

Switches the vehicle from the direct drivetrain (wheel torque applied straight from [member throttle]) to the PhysX engine drivetrain: an engine (torque curve, [member engine_peak_torque], idle/max omega) driving through a clutch and a gearbox (reverse + neutral + forward ratios, [member gear_final_ratio], [member gear_switch_time], autobox). Forward gears drive the vehicle nose-first (-Z), the reverse gear drives it backward, and neutral coasts. Switching rebuilds the vehicle; the pose is kept.

constants.constant: Engine-drive gear index for reverse ([method get_engine_gear] reports it while reversing).
Engine-drive gear index for neutral: no drive torque reaches the wheels, so the car coasts on its inertia regardless of [member throttle].
Special [member target_gear] value for DRIVE: hand the forward gears to the autobox (requires [member use_autobox] for shifting; without it the gearbox just holds its current gear).
